title: Distribution, Installation, Completion, and Release Documentation

milestones.name: User-Local Installation Contract
pattern: Convention over Configuration, Shared Installation Layout
milestones.objective: Define one XDG-aware installation layout and reusable install behavior shared by source builds, release downloads, and shell completion.
milestones.success: All installation paths target ~/.local by default, support PREFIX overrides, avoid sudo by default, treat WSL2 as Linux, and agree on binary and completion destinations.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Source[Source checkout] --> Contract[Installation contract]
    Release[Release archive] --> Contract
    WSL[WSL2 Linux environment] --> Contract
    Contract --> Binary[User binary directory]
    Contract --> Bash[Bash completion directory]
    Contract --> Zsh[Zsh completion directory]

tasks.name: Define installation paths and platform support
tasks.what: Add a small installation helper contract for resolving user-local binary and completion destinations from PREFIX, HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, OS, and shell inputs.
tasks.why: Make, install.sh, and the CLI completion installer must use identical destinations and explicitly support Linux, WSL2, and macOS without duplicating path logic.
acceptance: Default prefix resolves to HOME/.local.
PREFIX overrides the default for source and system-wide installs.
XDG_DATA_HOME controls user completion data locations where applicable.
Linux and WSL2 resolve through the same Linux layout.
macOS resolves a documented user-local layout.
Unsupported native Windows returns a clear error.

tasks.name: Add PATH readiness and shell guidance
tasks.what: Add reusable checks that determine whether the installed binary directory is currently discoverable and produce shell-specific activation guidance.
tasks.why: Installers should make squid-os immediately understandable without silently or repeatedly editing shell startup files.
acceptance: PATH checks use path components rather than substring matching.
Bash and Zsh guidance names the correct startup profile and restart command.
WSL2 Bash receives normal Linux guidance.
No helper silently edits .bashrc, .profile, or .zshrc.
Repeated checks remain idempotent and produce stable output.

tasks.name: Add cross-platform installation contract tests
tasks.what: Add table-driven fixtures covering Linux, WSL2, macOS, XDG overrides, custom PREFIX values, missing HOME, and unsupported platforms.
tasks.why: The installation contract is security- and usability-sensitive and must remain consistent before Make, shell scripts, and CLI commands depend on it.
acceptance: Tests cover Linux amd64 and arm64 layouts.
Tests identify WSL2 but preserve Linux artifact and path behavior.
Tests cover macOS amd64 and arm64 layouts.
Tests cover paths containing spaces.
Tests cover missing or malformed environment values with clear failures.

milestones.name: Source Install and Shell Completion
milestones.objective: Make a source checkout install a production binary and shell completion into the shared user-local layout, with explicit uninstall behavior and no default sudo requirement.
milestones.success: make install builds and installs squid-os under ~/.local by default, completion install and uninstall work for Bash and Zsh, raw Cobra generation remains available, and repeated operations are safe.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
    Checkout[Git checkout] --> Make[make install]
    Make --> Build[Versioned binary]
    Make --> Complete[Completion installer]
    Build --> Prefix[Selected prefix]
    Complete --> Bash[Bash completion]
    Complete --> Zsh[Zsh completion]
    Prefix --> Verify[Installation verification]

tasks.name: Implement user-local Make install lifecycle
tasks.what: Replace the fallback-copy Makefile with explicit build, install, uninstall, completion, clean, test, and verify targets using PREFIX and DESTDIR.
tasks.why: Source users need deterministic installation without hidden sudo attempts or fallback destinations.
snippet:
BINARY := squid-os
PREFIX ?= $(HOME)/.local
DESTDIR ?=
BINDIR := $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin

.PHONY: build install uninstall completion test verify clean

install: build
	# Install binary and detected-shell completion into the shared layout.

uninstall:
	# Remove only files owned by squid-os installation.
acceptance: make build embeds the canonical version and git commit metadata.
make install defaults to HOME/.local/bin/squid-os.
make install PREFIX=/usr/local supports an explicit system-wide destination.
DESTDIR supports packaging without changing logical PREFIX.
make install creates missing destination directories.
make uninstall removes the binary and installed completion without deleting unrelated directories.
No Make target silently invokes sudo.

tasks.name: Add completion install and uninstall commands
tasks.what: Extend the Cobra completion command with install and uninstall subcommands for Bash and Zsh, using the shared installation layout and optional shell auto-detection.
tasks.why: Users should not need to redirect generated scripts manually, while package managers must retain raw completion generation.
acceptance: squid-os completion install auto-detects Bash or Zsh from SHELL.
squid-os completion install bash and zsh work explicitly.
squid-os completion uninstall removes the matching completion file.
Raw squid-os completion bash and zsh continue writing scripts to stdout.
Installation uses atomic file replacement and creates parent directories.
The command prints the installed path and any required shell restart guidance.
The completion command never modifies PATH or shell startup files.

tasks.name: Integrate and test source installation end to end
tasks.what: Wire Make installation to generated completion artifacts and add an isolated-prefix smoke test for install, repeat install, command execution, completion presence, and uninstall.
tasks.why: The source workflow must prove that binary and completion installation operate together without touching the developer machine during CI.
snippet:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Install into a temporary PREFIX.
# Verify binary version and completion files.
# Repeat installation to prove idempotence.
# Uninstall and verify owned files are removed.
acceptance: The smoke test installs entirely under a temporary directory.
The installed binary runs --version and --help successfully.
Bash and Zsh completion files are generated from the installed binary.
A second install succeeds without duplicate files or profile changes.
Uninstall leaves unrelated sentinel files untouched.
The test runs on Linux and WSL2 without sudo.

milestones.name: Release Binary Installer
milestones.objective: Replace the source-building install.sh with a stable downloader that selects a published artifact, verifies it, installs user-locally, and installs completion.
milestones.success: curl install.sh downloads the correct Linux, WSL2, or macOS artifact, verifies authenticated release metadata when available and SHA-256 integrity always, installs without sudo by default, and provides exact PATH activation guidance.
milestones.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Script as install.sh
    participant Release as GitHub Release
    participant Local as User local prefix
    User->>Script: Run installer
    Script->>Script: Detect OS architecture shell WSL2
    Script->>Release: Download archive metadata checksum signature
    Script->>Script: Verify provenance and checksum
    Script->>Local: Atomically install binary
    Script->>Local: Install shell completion
    Script-->>User: Print version paths and activation steps

tasks.name: Resolve release version and platform artifact
tasks.what: Rewrite install.sh detection and release resolution for latest or pinned versions across Linux, WSL2, and macOS on amd64 and arm64.
tasks.why: The downloader must select one deterministic published artifact and fail clearly on unsupported systems before making changes.
snippet:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# Inputs: SQUID_OS_VERSION, SQUID_OS_PREFIX, SQUID_OS_GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
# Detect linux or darwin and amd64 or arm64.
# Treat WSL2 as linux and select the linux artifact.
# Resolve latest release only when no version is pinned.
acceptance: Linux amd64 and arm64 map to matching release archives.
WSL2 amd64 and arm64 map to Linux release archives.
macOS amd64 and arm64 map to Darwin release archives.
SQUID_OS_VERSION pins a specific tag without querying latest.
Repository and download base can be overridden for deterministic tests and mirrors.
Native Windows and unsupported architectures fail before downloading.
The script is POSIX shell compatible or clearly requires Bash with a validated interpreter.

tasks.name: Verify release integrity and authenticity
tasks.what: Download release checksums and verification metadata, authenticate them when supported, and verify the selected archive before extraction.
tasks.why: Checksums catch corruption, while signatures or CI provenance provide a stronger trust signal against artifact substitution.
snippet:
# Verification policy
# 1. Verify signed checksum or release attestation when the configured tool is available.
# 2. Always verify the selected archive against checksums.txt.
# 3. Fail closed on mismatch, malformed metadata, or missing checksum entry.
# 4. Document the curl installer bootstrap trust boundary.
acceptance: CI-generated checksums.txt is mandatory for installation.
The selected archive SHA-256 must match exactly before extraction.
The installer supports sha256sum and macOS shasum -a 256.
Checksum mismatch, missing entry, and malformed metadata stop installation without replacing an existing binary.
The plan selects and documents either GitHub artifact attestations, Cosign, or Minisign as the authenticity mechanism.
The public verification identity or key and rotation procedure are documented outside release artifacts.
Documentation explains that curl-pipe-shell still trusts the fetched installer.

tasks.name: Install release binary and completion safely
tasks.what: Install the verified binary atomically under the selected prefix, install completion for the detected shell, and report activation or PATH guidance.
tasks.why: A successful download must produce the same predictable layout as make install without leaving partial upgrades or surprising profile edits.
snippet:
#!/bin/sh

# Extract into a temporary directory.
# Validate the binary with --version.
# Atomically replace PREFIX/bin/squid-os.
# Generate and install completion using the installed binary.
# Print exact activation guidance without silently editing profiles.
acceptance: Default installation uses HOME/.local and requires no sudo.
SQUID_OS_PREFIX supports an explicit alternative destination.
Existing installations remain intact if download, verification, extraction, or validation fails.
Bash or Zsh completion is installed when the shell is recognized.
Unknown shells still install the binary and print manual completion instructions.
The final output reports installed version, binary path, completion path, and whether PATH is ready.
Repeated installation and upgrades are idempotent.
Temporary files are cleaned on success, failure, and interruption.

tasks.name: Test release installer against local fixtures
tasks.what: Build local release fixtures and exercise install.sh through a local HTTP server for supported platforms, pinned/latest versions, upgrades, failures, and rollback.
tasks.why: Installer regressions must be reproducible in CI without mutating user directories or relying on GitHub availability.
snippet:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Build fake archives and checksum metadata.
# Serve fixtures from localhost.
# Run install.sh with isolated HOME and PREFIX.
# Assert success, rejection, rollback, cleanup, and completion behavior.
acceptance: Tests cover Linux amd64 and arm64 artifact names.
Tests cover WSL2 selecting Linux artifacts through injectable detection fixtures.
Tests cover Darwin amd64 and arm64 artifact names without requiring macOS execution.
Tests cover pinned and mocked-latest releases.
Tests cover checksum mismatch, missing metadata, HTTP failure, invalid archive, and invalid binary rollback.
Tests prove the installer never writes outside isolated HOME, PREFIX, and temporary directories.

milestones.name: Continuous Integration and Release Automation
pattern: Reproducible Build, Tagged Release Pipeline, Supply Chain Attestation
milestones.objective: Validate every change and publish reproducible Linux and macOS release archives, checksums, provenance, and release notes from version tags.
milestones.success: Pull requests run code and installer gates; version tags produce amd64 and arm64 artifacts for Linux and macOS; checksums and attestations are published automatically; no release script is rewritten per version.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Change[Push or pull request] --> CI[Validation workflow]
    CI --> Go[Build test vet]
    CI --> Shell[Shell lint and installer fixtures]
    Tag[Version tag] --> Release[Release workflow]
    Release --> Matrix[Linux Darwin amd64 arm64]
    Matrix --> Archives[Versioned archives]
    Archives --> Checksums[Checksums]
    Archives --> Provenance[Attestations]
    Checksums --> GitHub[GitHub Release]
    Provenance --> GitHub

tasks.name: Add continuous integration quality gates
tasks.what: Add a GitHub Actions workflow for Go build/test/vet, formatting checks, shell lint, source-install smoke tests, and release-installer fixture tests.
tasks.why: Installation and release code needs the same mandatory validation as application code before merge.
snippet:
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  go:
    # Build, test, vet, and formatting checks.
  install:
    # ShellCheck and isolated installer tests.
acceptance: CI runs on pushes and pull requests.
CI runs go build, go test, go vet, and gofmt verification.
CI runs ShellCheck on maintained shell scripts.
CI runs source and release installer tests in isolated directories.
CI uses pinned major action versions and least-privilege permissions.
make verify reproduces the primary CI checks locally.

tasks.name: Configure reproducible cross-platform releases
tasks.what: Add GoReleaser configuration for static Linux and macOS amd64 and arm64 binaries, deterministic archives, checksums, changelog generation, and version metadata.
tasks.why: Release artifacts must match install.sh naming exactly and be generated consistently from tags rather than developer machines.
snippet:
version: 2

builds:
  - id: squid-os
    binary: squid-os
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt
acceptance: Artifacts are produced for linux amd64, linux arm64, darwin amd64, and darwin arm64.
Archive names exactly match install.sh resolution rules.
Builds use CGO_ENABLED=0 unless a verified platform dependency requires otherwise.
Version and git commit metadata derive from the release tag and commit.
checksums.txt includes every published archive.
Snapshot releases can be generated locally without publishing.

tasks.name: Publish tagged releases with provenance
tasks.what: Add a tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow that validates, runs GoReleaser, publishes artifacts and checksums, and emits the selected authenticity metadata.
tasks.why: Users need automatic releases whose artifacts can be verified by install.sh and traced to an authorized CI workflow.
snippet:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

jobs:
  release:
    # Validate tag and tests.
    # Build and publish through GoReleaser.
    # Publish GitHub artifact attestations or selected signatures.
acceptance: Only semantic version tags matching the documented policy publish releases.
The workflow runs tests before publishing.
GitHub permissions are scoped to the release job and required capabilities.
Archives, checksums.txt, and authenticity metadata appear on one GitHub Release.
Release notes are generated consistently and can be edited before final publication when configured.
The workflow fails if expected artifacts or verification metadata are missing.
The install script does not need modification for each version.

tasks.name: Validate release artifacts and installer compatibility
tasks.what: Add a CI dry-run job that inspects snapshot archives, verifies checksums and version metadata, and installs the host-compatible artifact through install.sh fixtures.
tasks.why: GoReleaser and install.sh can each pass independently while disagreeing on names or archive contents; this test closes that integration gap.
snippet:
# Release compatibility checks
# - Build snapshot artifacts.
# - Assert the complete OS and architecture name matrix.
# - Verify archive contents and checksums.
# - Serve artifacts locally and run install.sh.
# - Execute the installed binary.
acceptance: The expected four release archives are present.
Each archive contains a squid-os executable and required release metadata only.
Every archive has a checksums.txt entry.
The installed host artifact reports the snapshot version and commit.
Any artifact naming drift between GoReleaser and install.sh fails CI.

milestones.name: Getting Started and Maintainer Documentation
pattern: Documentation as Product, Single Source of Truth
milestones.objective: Replace outdated startup documentation with a concise first-run path, source and release installation guidance, WSL2 support, completion behavior, upgrades, uninstall, and maintainer release procedures.
milestones.success: A new user can install and run Squid-OS from README alone; WSL2 status and native Windows scope are explicit; maintainers can cut and verify a release; website download guidance matches the repository.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Visitor[New visitor] --> README[README quick start]
    README --> Curl[Curl release install]
    README --> Source[Source make install]
    README --> WSL[WSL2 guidance]
    Curl --> FirstRun[First run]
    Source --> FirstRun
    WSL --> FirstRun
    Maintainer[Maintainer] --> ReleaseDoc[Release runbook]
    ReleaseDoc --> Tag[Tag and publish]
    Tag --> Verify[Verify release and installer]

tasks.name: Rewrite README quick start and installation guide
tasks.what: Rewrite the README opening, prerequisites, installation, first run, CLI examples, completion, upgrade, uninstall, configuration, and platform support sections.
tasks.why: The current README documents removed headless/incognito flags, obsolete files, a source-building installer, and stale Go requirements.
snippet:
# Squid-OS

<!-- Product summary and current screenshot -->

## Install

### Release binary
```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gogluejf/squid-os/master/install.sh | sh
```

### Build from source
```sh
git clone https://github.com/gogluejf/squid-os.git
cd squid-os
make install
```

## First run
```sh
squid-os
squid-os run --prompt "hello"
```
acceptance: README leads with a concise product description and valid screenshot path.
Release installation and source installation are distinct and accurate.
README documents HOME/.local default, PATH guidance, PREFIX override, upgrade, and uninstall.
README documents automatic and manual Bash/Zsh completion installation.
README explicitly supports Linux, WSL2, and macOS and states native Windows is unsupported.
CLI examples use current tui and run grammar with no removed flags.
Referenced source files and commands exist.
Security wording explains checksum/provenance verification and curl installer trust.

tasks.name: Document platform support and installation troubleshooting
tasks.what: Add a focused installation document covering Linux, WSL2, macOS, shell discovery, PATH activation, completion locations, custom prefixes, proxies, and common failures.
tasks.why: The README should stay concise while users still need precise recovery steps for environment-specific installation issues.
snippet:
# Installation

## Supported platforms
- Linux amd64 and arm64
- WSL2 amd64 and arm64 using Linux artifacts
- macOS amd64 and arm64
- Native Windows not currently supported

## Troubleshooting
<!-- PATH, shell completion, permissions, proxies, checksum failures, custom prefixes -->
acceptance: WSL2 instructions explain that it uses Linux artifacts and installs inside the Linux filesystem.
Documentation recommends cloning/building inside the WSL filesystem rather than mounted Windows paths for performance.
Bash and Zsh completion paths and reload commands are documented.
Custom PREFIX, XDG_DATA_HOME, and noninteractive environment variables are documented.
Troubleshooting covers command not found, completion not loading, permission errors, verification failures, and unsupported platforms.
No documentation recommends sudo for the default user-local install.

tasks.name: Add maintainer release runbook
tasks.what: Document versioning, pre-release checks, tag creation, automated publication, artifact verification, installer smoke tests, rollback, and verification-identity maintenance.
tasks.why: Release automation is only reliable when maintainers have an explicit operational and security procedure.
snippet:
# Releasing Squid-OS

## Before tagging
```sh
make verify
make release-snapshot
```

## Publish
```sh
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

## Verify
<!-- GitHub Release artifacts, checksums, attestations, and install.sh smoke test -->
acceptance: The runbook defines the semantic version and tag policy.
The runbook requires a clean tree and passing local verification before tagging.
The runbook explains the automated workflow and expected artifact matrix.
The runbook includes post-release install.sh verification for latest and pinned versions.
Rollback or yanking guidance avoids silently replacing immutable release artifacts.
Authenticity identity/key rotation and compromise response are documented.

tasks.name: Align website downloads and validate documentation
tasks.what: Update website installation/download guidance to match README and add automated checks for stale commands, local links, referenced files, and release URLs.
tasks.why: Multiple public installation surfaces must not diverge as the CLI and release workflow evolve.
snippet:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Validate local Markdown links and referenced paths.
# Reject removed CLI flags and obsolete installer commands.
# Check that documented release artifact names match configuration.
acceptance: Website download instructions show release install and source make install separately.
Website states Linux, WSL2, macOS, architecture support, and native Windows scope accurately.
Website completion and PATH wording matches README.
Documentation checks reject removed --headless and CLI --incognito examples.
Documentation checks validate local README/docs links and referenced files.
make docs-check runs locally and in CI.

problem: Squid-OS currently has a source-only installer, a system-first Makefile install target, generated-but-uninstalled shell completion, outdated README instructions, and no automated multi-platform release pipeline. Users need one predictable installation experience whether they download a release, build from source, or run under WSL2.
goal: User-local make install and uninstall workflows, a secure release-binary install.sh, friendly Bash and Zsh completion installation, explicit WSL2 support, automated Linux and macOS release artifacts, checksums and provenance, CI validation, and an accurate getting-started README.
